facts.text: Henry County, Virginia lists 19 sites on the National Register of Historic Places, including five of statewide significance.
The county’s historic architecture showcases Colonial Revival, Classical Revival, and Greek Revival styles, reflecting its 18th‑ and 19th‑century heritage.
The Carter, John Waddey House, built in the late 1700s, is one of the county’s oldest surviving homes and appears on the National Register.
The historic district of Fieldale preserves buildings from the 1900‑1940 era, once a bustling textile town with rail‑related structures.
Eltham Manor, a Greek Revival house built in the mid‑1800s, is listed on the National Register and exemplifies the county’s architectural diversity.
Grassdale Farm, added to the National Register in 2002, reflects the county’s agricultural heritage and includes a historic farmhouse.
